brief.subject: IRS finalizes rules for paying taxes directly by card
brief.headline: IRS Finalizes Rules Letting It Take Card Payments for Taxes Directly
brief.dek: New final rules let the IRS accept credit and debit cards without a middleman, plus a data center tax push and a corporate spin-off rule change.
brief.lede: Final IRS regulations allow the agency to accept credit and debit card tax payments directly, with no third-party payment processor required.

sections.heading: IRS can now take cards directly
bullets: Final regulations let the IRS accept credit and debit card tax payments itself, without sending taxpayers to outside processors.
The rules implement Taxpayer First Act changes, so card payment options for business taxes may shift.
Restrictions on the IRS paying fees under card-payment contracts are removed, which could change who absorbs processing costs.
Owners who pay estimated or business taxes by card should watch for updated IRS payment options.

sections.heading: Wyden targets data centers with taxes
bullets: Sen. Ron Wyden, top Democrat on Senate Finance, proposed an excise tax on data centers.
The same proposal would exclude data centers from certain tax breaks.
A companion bill would provide aid to displaced workers.
These are proposals only; nothing changes for businesses unless Congress acts.

sections.heading: IRS pulls back part of spin-off rules
bullets: The IRS partially withdrew proposed Section 355 regulations on tax-free distributions of controlled corporation stock.
The withdrawn portion covers the device prohibition and the active trade or business requirement.
Closely held corporations weighing a split-up and their shareholders should check how the change affects planning.

brief.seo_description: IRS final rules allow direct credit and debit card tax payments, Wyden proposes data center taxes, and the IRS partly withdraws Section 355 proposals.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Guidance Under Section 355 Concerning Device and Active Trade or Business; Partial Withdrawal
items.snippet: This document partially withdraws a notice of proposed rulemaking containing proposed regulations regarding the application of the device prohibition and the active trade or business requirement for distributions of controlled corporation stock (or stock and securities) by a distributing corporation without income, gain, or loss. The proposed regulations would affect corporations and their shareholders and security holders.

items.title: Rule: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means. The final regulations reflect changes to the law made by the Taxpayer First Act that would allow the IRS to directly accept payments of tax by credit or debit card, without having to connect taxpayers to third-party payment processors. These final regulations remove restrictions on the payment of any fee by the IRS under any contracts related to payment of taxes by credit, debit, or charge car
